What is it costing you now?

Not what Ordence costs — that comes as one fixed number after a written scope. This is the other side of the sum, and most businesses have never actually done it. Change the figures to yours; the working is shown underneath.

Your numbers

Everything below starts at a plausible default for a business of forty people. Nothing is sent anywhere — this runs entirely in your browser.

Roughly what it costs you a year—

This is arithmetic, not a forecast, and it is your arithmetic — we do not know your business. It says what the current way of working costs. What Ordence costs is a separate conversation and comes as one fixed number after a written scope. If the figure above is smaller than a subscription would be, that is a genuine answer and you should not buy anything.

Why these five things and not others

A calculator that lets you add up anything gives you a number you cannot defend. These are the five costs that show up in almost every business of this size, that people can estimate honestly, and that a single ledger genuinely changes.

  • Re-keying. The same figure typed into a second system, by somebody paid to do something else. It is the most boring line here and usually the largest.
  • Month-end. Not the accounting — the reconciliation before the accounting can start. One ledger does not shorten your books; it removes the argument about which system was right.
  • Stock written off. Only the part that went wrong because the number was wrong. If you do not hold stock, set it to zero and the sum still works.
  • Input tax credit. Claimed and reversed, or never claimed because nobody opened GSTR-2B in time. This is real money and it is invisible until an audit.
  • What is NOT here: revenue you might win, deals you might close faster, customers you might keep. Those are real and we cannot estimate them for you, so putting them in would only make the total less believable.

Now get the other number.

A written scope, the modules it needs, and one fixed price — usually inside a business day. Then you have both sides of the sum.
